description: Edits a training module as its page does (owner or admin seats only): title, description, atom_order, context_position (before or after), status draft or published. Publishing puts it on the team's own training page (nothing is sent) and is refused until every atom has quiz questions (generate_training_questions). To add something to training ("add that to new-hire training"): read training_modules for the module the person means (by title and description), find or create the handbook article that holds the text (search sops first, as the handbook tools say), then send atom_order as the module's current order with that article id placed where it belongs; an article already in atom_order needs only its article edited. A module that gains an atom needs questions for it (generate_training_questions) before it can be published again. Before adding anything to the handbook, search the sops read entity by the topic (search finds by meaning): when an article already covers it, put the new text into that article (edit_handbook_article with its full content_md, the new lines placed where they belong, or draft_handbook_edit) instead of a new one; create a new article only when none fits, and say which closest article you found and why it did not fit. Audience comes from the person's words: cleaner SOPs, cleaning standards or staff = cleaner; policies, office or VA = va; when the words do not say, ask in one line. Ask which place, in one line naming both, when two places fit the person's words equally well: two articles, or two training modules that both match (two new-hire modules are a tie whatever their status, draft or published); a place the person named outright is never a tie. The proposed change is the confirmation, so never ask "should I add this?" first. Pass the same idempotency_key when retrying.

idempotency_key.description: Your id for this operation (8-128 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -). Reuse it on every retry of the same operation; use a new one for a new operation.

name: edit_training_module
